mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, compressing discount rates on equity cash flows and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive over 20 days despite FEDFUNDS rising, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) above 140,000 signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive within 5 days despite PAYEMS exceeding 140,000, or the increase is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in the federal funds rate below 0.2% and robust growth in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 14,000 indicate accommodative monetary policy and strong demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive over 60 days when both FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 meet the trigger condition, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, sustained federal funds rates below 2% signal accommodative policy, compressing discount rates and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive over 60 days when FEDFUNDS remains below 2% in the late-cycle expansion regime, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) by over 10% from the previous month signals labor market weakening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive within 5 days despite PAYEMS increasing by over 10% from the previous month, or the increase is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 97 signals supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive over 20 days despite INDPRO falling below 97, or the drop is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: Rising personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) alongside falling federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) below 0.2% indicate accommodative policy and strong demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive over 60 days when both GDPC1 exceeds 14,000 and FEDFUNDS falls below 0.2, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, a sustained decline in unemployment rates (UNRATE) below 6% signals labor market improvement, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive over 20 days when UNRATE falls below 6% in the post-shock recovery regime, or the effect is not statistically significant.
